about: Pahlmeyer was founded by Jayson Pahlmeyer, a trial attorney who set out in the 1980s to make a “California Mouton.” After consulting soil experts at the University of Bordeaux and sourcing Bordeaux clones, he released his first Proprietary Red in 1986, with Randy Dunn and later Helen Turley among the winemakers who shaped the house. The Jayson label, named for him, followed in 1992. E. & J. Gallo bought the Pahlmeyer and Jayson brands in 2019, and in 2020 the winery moved into the former William Hill estate on Atlas Peak Road.

Jayson is Pahlmeyer’s more approachable bottling, blending mountain-grown and valley-floor fruit and made to drink well young. The 2021 is a Merlot-led Bordeaux blend: 76% Merlot, with Cabernet Sauvignon, Malbec, Petit Verdot and a dash of Cabernet Franc. Pahlmeyer describes it as rich and fleshy, with mountain Merlot at its core. Fruit sources for the house include the high-elevation Waters Ranch on Atlas Peak, planted by David Abreu, and hillside sites in eastern Napa.

The winemaker describes crushed black cherry, mushroom and leather on the nose, then ripe black cherry and black currant with mocha and toasty spice, a plush middle and smooth, polished tannins. James Suckling called it lovely to drink now as a young wine. Wine Enthusiast suggests drinking it through 2032, so it has room to develop, though it is already open and generous.
facts: 76% Merlot, 12% Cabernet Sauvignon, 7% Malbec, 4% Petit Verdot, 1% Cabernet Franc
